04b_1_square_roots_2x2.png: Eigenvalues of two $2 \times 2$ square roots, for $q = 1$ and $p$ from $-3$ to $3$ (pure numbers). Left: $p\sigma_x + \sigma_z$ squares to $(p^2 + 1) I_2$, and its eigenvalues are always the two real numbers $\pm\sqrt{p^2 + 1}$. Right: $p\sigma_x + N$ squares to $(p^2 - 1) I_2$; its eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{p^2 - 1}$ are real for $|p| > 1$ (solid line, the real part of the positive one) and imaginary for $|p| < 1$ (dashed line, the imaginary part): a minus sign in the quadratic form makes the root imaginary when the minus term wins.
